sentences.text: Shri Manish Datt Senior Advocate along with Shri Ratna Bharat Tiwari, learned counsel for the appellant.
Mr. Satya Pal Chadar-G.A. appearing on behalf of Advocate General for the State.
Heard on admission.
Appeal being arguable is admitted for hearing.
Also heard on I.A. No. 8455/2022 an application under Section 389(1) of the Cr.P.C. for suspension of remaining jail sentence and grant of bail to appellant.

T he appellant has been convicted under Section 376 (1) of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 10 years with fine of Rs.1,000/- and under Section 506-II of IPC and sentenced to undergo RI for 1 year with fine of Rs.1,000/- with default stipulations.

Learned senior counsel for the appellant after referring to Ex.P/9, statement of prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. and Ex.D/1, statement recorded under Section 161 of Cr.P.C. of prosecutrix as well as deposition of PW-8 submits that prosecutrix was a married woman and her husband has turned out from his house as per above documents.
Prosecutrix is a consenting party.
Appellant is in jail since 03.09.2022 and he is an innocent person.
He has been falsely implicated in this case.
The final hearing of this appeal is not possible in near future.
He further submits that there is no evidence against the appellant.
On above grounds, it is prayed that remaining jail 2 CRA-8170-2022 sentence of appellant may be suspended and he be released on bail.
The prayer is opposed by learned counsel for the State.
In view of Ex.P/9, Ex. D/1 and deposition of prosecutrix (PW-8), I deem it proper to suspend the remaining jail sentence of the present appellant.
Accordingly, aforesaid I.A. is allowed.
